import pandas as pd

# Analyze Season 2 class performance and timing of the peak
trips = tables['trips']

# Filter to season 2 only
s2_trips = trips[trips['fished_date_season'] == 2]

# Class performance by day-of-year range
# Calculate average YT per trip by class
class_perf = s2_trips.groupby('cls').agg({
    'yt': 'mean',
    'cls': 'count'
}).rename(columns={'cls': 'trip_count'})
class_perf.columns = ['avg_yt_per_trip', 'num_trips']
class_perf = class_perf.sort_values('avg_yt_per_trip', ascending=False)

print("=== Season 2 Class Performance ===")
print(class_perf)
print()

# Find when the peak actually occurred - look at daily avg YT by day-of-year for multi-day classes
multi_day_classes = ['day_1_5', 'overnight', 'full_day']
s2_multi = s2_trips[s2_trips['cls'].isin(multi_day_classes)]

# Daily average YT per trip
daily_perf = s2_multi.groupby('fished_date_doy').agg({
    'yt': ['sum', 'count', 'mean'],
    'anglers': 'sum'
})
daily_perf.columns = ['total_yt', 'num_trips', 'avg_yt_per_trip', 'total_anglers']
daily_perf['avg_yt_per_angler'] = daily_perf['total_yt'] / daily_perf['total_anglers']

# Find peak window (highest 3-day rolling average)
daily_perf['rolling_3d_avg'] = daily_perf['avg_yt_per_trip'].rolling(window=3, center=True).mean()
peak_window = daily_perf['rolling_3d_avg'].idxmax()
print(f"=== Season 2 Multi-Day Peak Window ===")
print(f"Peak DOY: {peak_window}")
print(f"Days 260-290 rolling 3-day average:")
peak_range = daily_perf.loc[260:290, ['total_yt', 'num_trips', 'avg_yt_per_trip', 'rolling_3d_avg']].dropna()
print(peak_range.head(20))
print()

})
